style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, 50mm prime lens overhead at f/8 for razor-sharp edge-to-edge focus. Extreme asymmetric flat-lay composition with generous negative space on the right. A heavy, textured rag-paper legal dossier lies open on a dark polished oak desk. The paper features muted, illegibly cropped schematic routing lines. Resting on the bottom left corner of the dossier is a solid brass vintage date-stamp, throwing a deep contact shadow. Even diffused daylight from a single window to the left, muted paper tones, quiet confidence, editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: text, typography, watermark, letters, numbers, logo, signature, words
rationale: A document flatlay perfectly captures the regulatory and evidentiary nature of the story, transforming the abstract concept of software logs into physical, legal proof anchored by time.
subject: an open legal dossier with system schematics anchored by a brass date-stamp
core_thesis: An AI agent's log is only legally viable evidence if it serves as a complete, replayable record of its decisions and is retained for the longest applicable regulatory period.
core_conflict: Transient, incomplete system logs vs. durable, replayable regulatory evidence spanning years.
